newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Apprail finds FCL lumber transfer fair.
newsitem.headline: Apprail finds FCL lumber transfer fair.

text.p: The NZ$93 million transfer of the Tasman Lumber operations between two Fletcher Challenge divisions is fair, according to an independent appraisal reported by the New Zealand Press Association on Monday.
Shareholders will be asked to approve the transaction at the group's October 31 annual meeting.
If consent is given, the transfer from Fletcher Building to Fletcher Forests will be effective retrospectively from July 1.

The asset was not placed within Fletcher Forests ahead of Fletcher's split into letter stocks earlier this year because of an outstanding dispute over Tasman's long-term logging contracts with the Forestry Corporation.
In its appraisal, First New Zealand Capital estimated the net replacement cost of the Tasman Lumber and HT Plywood mill for Fletcher Forests at between $111 million and $139 million.

The broker, however, was unable to determine whether the alternative action of buying other existing processing plants would result in more or less value being generated for Fletcher Forests than from buying the processing assets.
But the report noted that control of processing capacity was considered by Fletcher Forests to be imperative to the implementation of its resource-to-customer chain strategy.
"In Fletcher Forests' view, it will result in incremental value in excess of the $93 million cost of purchasing the processing assets."
First New Zealand Capital also found the transaction fair to Fletcher Building.
"We estimate the total value of the processing asset to Fletcher Building under its management and on an autonomous going concern basis to be in the range of $18 million and $71 million," it said.
Furthermore, the value likely to be realised from closing the processing plants and liquidating the processing assets was estimated to be between $38 million and $43 million.

"We consider Fletcher Forests is the party that is most likely to extract the highest expected value from the processing assets and hence, on the basis of being a willing buyer, Fletcher Forest should be prepared to pay the highest price for
"We would expect there to be a very limited buyer audience that could justify paying a comparable price to that to be paid by Fletcher Forests," the report said.
